problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $A(1,1,0)$ and $B(3,-1,2).$
worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $A$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=a+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $a$ is the position vector of $A.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $A(1,1,0)$ and $B(3,-1,2)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{AB} \\  & =⟨3,-1,2⟩-⟨1,1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-2,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
